page: Amazon Web Services t8i.medium is a burstable performance instance powered by an Intel processor. It features the x86_64 CPU architecture with 2 virtual CPUs (vCPUs) derived from 1 physical core, supporting 2 threads per core. The processor operates at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The instance is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core.

This server operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It does not include any local storage, meaning all storage must be network-attached. The baseline network bandwidth is rated at 0 Gbps, and the instance does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses. There are no dedicated graphics processing units (GPUs) bundled with this configuration.

The t8i.medium utilizes a burstable CPU allocation model, which is designed to handle temporary spikes in CPU demand while maintaining a lower baseline performance during idle periods. This resource profile makes it a cost-efficient option for workloads with variable CPU utilization, such as small-scale web servers, development environments, microservices, and code repositories. However, the lack of local storage and baseline network bandwidth limits its suitability for data-intensive or high-throughput production databases.
